name: Being strong and hiding distress
what_people_do: Carry on, keep distress private, and avoid asking for help; a cultural legacy of strength.
why_they_say_it_works: Strength was needed to survive; showing weakness is seen as risky or shameful.

documented_by.source: Sisley EJ et al 2011, Health Soc Care Community, PMID 21314849
documented_by.quote_or_summary: London, 7 African Caribbean women: gender roles and a cultural legacy of being strong and hiding distress shaped how they managed difficulties; younger generations more open to professional help.

evidence.finding: Qualitative; the strong-woman norm affects help-seeking; no outcome test.

source.name: Sisley EJ et al 2011, Health Soc Care Community, PMID 21314849

harm_note: Delayed help-seeking is the harm identified.
